source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 ("Sion tops the poll: rural elections with 96 pc"); Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1967, p. 2 ("Poll surprises in many areas"); Ballymena Observer, 8 June 1967, p. 8 ("At Antrim")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Votes and divisions read from the Belfast Telegraph's rural results table of 2 June 1967, checked against the News-Letter of the same date. Read on the page images: the Telegraph prints 'Antrim Rural-Jack Bleakley (U.) 680; Lieut.-Comdr. R. W. Rutherford-Browne (Ratepayers' Association) 479. Unionist majority 201' (680 - 479 = 201); the News-Letter prints the winner as 'Jack Blakeley'.

note: Triennial election of rural district councillors, polled on Thursday 1 June 1967. Four divisions were contested; the remaining divisions were filled without opposition and their names were not printed in the reports used here. Unionist majority 201.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page images of the Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 and the Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1967, p. 2 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the winner's surname is now Bleakley as the Telegraph prints it (was Blakely, which neither paper prints; the News-Letter has Blakeley), and the printed majority 201 is recorded. Corrected from the page image of the Ballymena Observer, 8 June 1967, p. 8 (w8-review, Nov 2026): the winner's surname is now Blakeley, as the Observer and the Belfast News-Letter print it (was Bleakley, the Belfast Telegraph's form); the Observer confirms 680, 479 and the majority of 201.
